title: A 'postal code must be 5 digits' check rejects every UK and Canadian address
assumption: A postal/zip code is always a short string of digits.

input.description: A postal code field validated against a fixed numeric pattern, written with only US ZIP codes in mind.

what_goes_wrong: Perfectly valid UK and Canadian postal codes are rejected outright because they mix letters and digits and don't match a 5-digit pattern at all.
why: US ZIP codes happen to be exactly 5 digits, but that's a US-specific format, not a property of 'postal codes' in general. UK postcodes (like SW1A 1AA) and Canadian postal codes (like K1A 0B1) are alphanumeric by design, with letter-digit structures that a 5-digit-only regex has no way to match.

repros.code:
import re
pattern = re.compile(r"^\d{5}$")
for code in ["02134", "SW1A 1AA", "K1A 0B1"]:
    print(code, bool(pattern.match(code)))

fix: Validate postal codes per-country using that country's actual format (or accept any reasonably short alphanumeric string if the country isn't known), never a single 5-digit pattern applied worldwide.

sources.title: Michael Tandy: Falsehoods Programmers Believe About Addresses

test_cases.note: A valid UK postcode should be accepted by your postal-code field.
